An Italian painter, engineer and scientist of the Renaissance, often seen as the model of the all-round genius. He was born at Vinci, near Florence, the illegitimate son of a notary, and trained in the workshop of the sculptor Verrocchio.

He worked in Florence, in Milan for Duke Ludovico Sforza, in Rome, and at the end of his life in France for King Francis I, dying at Amboise in 1519. He finished few paintings, but they include:

  • The Last Supper in Milan, painted in the 1490s;
  • the Mona Lisa, begun around 1503;
  • The Virgin of the Rocks and Lady with an Ermine.

His notebooks, thousands of pages in mirror writing, hold studies of anatomy from dissections, flying machines, water, rocks and weapons. Few of his inventions were built and his notes were not published, so his science had little effect in his own time. His soft shading and close study of nature changed painting. He knew, and competed with, the younger Michelangelo.
